_note: v2 hook overrides for le Pont des Contraires (B57_pont). Every hook describes what is actually painted (nothing is written in the paintings).

fr_petit_adj.hook: Like English 'petite', said puh-TEE: a tiny PET mouse sips TEA from a little cup on the bridge parapet, SMALL as a cork.
fr_petit_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: the painted mouse holds a small cup on the parapet.

fr_bon_adj.hook: A dog wags its tail at a GOOD, giant bone ("BOHN") on the bridge: "Good dog, good bone!"
fr_bon_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: the painted bone is a giant one lying on the parapet. Text pass 2026-10-28: bracketed respelling matched to the card (BON -> BOHN).

fr_grand_adj.hook: Like English 'grand', said GRAHN (d silent): a TALL giraffe beside the bridge has to bend so far to drink from the pond that she GROANS, she's so BIG.
fr_grand_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: the giraffe stands in the pond by the bridge.

fr_jeune_adj.hook: A YOUNG June bug ("ZHUHN") in a blue cap skateboards across the bridge.
fr_jeune_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: the painted June bug rides a skateboard; there is no old beetle.

fr_vieux_adj.hook: An OLD man in a deckchair admires the view ("VYEUH"), his long white beard spilling down his chest.
fr_vieux_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: his beard is long but does not reach his toes. Text pass 2026-10-28 (hook lint): respelling (VYUH) -> (VYEUH) to match the card.

fr_mauvais_adj.hook: A BAD mauve ("moh-VEH") hat with big teeth bites at the man trying it on.
fr_mauvais_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: the painted mauve hat has a toothy mouth and the man holds it up.

fr_nouveau_adj.hook: Like English 'nouveau', said noo-VOH: a kid shows off a NEW shiny red bike on the bridge: "NEW, WHOA!"

fr_froid_adj.hook: A 'FRAID cat ("FRWAH") in a striped scarf and woolly hat shivers in the COLD, its breath puffing white.

fr_ancien_adj.hook: "On sea, an ("ahn-SYAN") OLD ship": an ancient galleon hung with weed drifts on the pond behind the bridge.
fr_ancien_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: the galleon is weed-covered and floats on the park pond.

fr_chaud_adj.hook: A HOT show ("SHOH"): a fire-juggler sweats as he juggles flaming torches on the bridge, the air shimmering with heat.
fr_chaud_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: one fire-juggler is painted, in the open air.

fr_long_adj.hook: Like English 'long', said LOHN: a sausage dog so LONG he stretches right along the riverbank under the bridge.
fr_long_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: he lies along the bank, not across the bridge.

fr_bas_adj.hook: A sheep says "baa" ("BAH") from the LOW bottom step by the river.

fr_difficile_adj.hook: Like English 'difficult', said dee-fee-SEEL: a fisherman in a rowing boat tries to coax a grumpy SEAL in, but it's the most DIFFICULT passenger ever.

fr_facile_adj.hook: Like English 'facile', said fah-SEEL: a SEAL on a rock balances a ball on its nose and sings "FA!", it's so EASY.

fr_court_adj.hook: A very SHORT dachshund by a little tennis COURT can't reach the net; the racquet is taller than him.

fr_rapide_adj.hook: "rah-PEAD": RAPID! A cheetah zooms along the bank so RAPIDLY it is just a blur.

fr_haut_adj.hook: "OH!" ("OH") gasps a girl on top of the bridge as her kite flies HIGH into the sky.

fr_leger_adj.hook: A LIGHT feather quill rests on an open ledger ("lay-ZHAY") without moving the page.
fr_leger_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: the feather rests on the ledger on a little box.

fr_lourd_adj.hook: A fisherman has hooked a HEAVY iron kettlebell ("LOOR"): his rod bends double and it will not budge.
fr_lourd_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: the object was repainted from a spiky lure (read as a weapon) to a harmless iron kettlebell, so the hook now names the kettlebell.

fr_lent_adj.hook: A SLOW snail takes all day to cross the lawn ("LAHN") beside the bridge.

fr_plein_adj.hook: A PLANE ("PLAN") so FULL of suitcases that a giraffe has to stick its neck out of the top.
fr_plein_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: the giraffe's neck sticks out of the luggage on top of the plane.

fr_propre_adj.hook: A CLEAN stage prop ("PROPR"): an actor in a ruff polishes his crown until it sparkles and admires his OWN reflection in it.
fr_propre_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: the painted prop is a shiny crown held by the actor.

fr_sale_adj.hook: Sal ("SAHL") the pig rolls in mud: DIRTY from ear to tail.
fr_sale_adj.why: kept, matches the painting. Text pass 2026-10-28: bracketed respelling matched to the card (SAL -> SAHL).

fr_fort_adj.hook: Like English 'fort', said FOR: a STRONG man lifts a whole FORT above his head at the market.

fr_vide_adj.hook: An EMPTY fridge with its door open shows a picture of a roast on the door like a VIDEO ("VEED"): nothing inside but a lonely light.
fr_vide_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: the picture on the fridge door is painted, not a screen.

fr_riche_adj.hook: "REESH": REACH! A RICH gentleman in a top hat leans over the quay wall to REACH a gold coin floating in the water.
fr_riche_adj.why: Top-hat cat replaced by a gentleman.

fr_pauvre_adj.hook: "POHVR": POOR puss! The rain POURS on a POOR thin gray cat sitting beside its empty saucer.
fr_pauvre_adj.why: Natural cat (no clothes); POOR/POURS sound-alikes on the item.

fr_ouvert_adj.hook: "oo-VEHR": "Oo, VERY nice!" gasps a little girl at the OPEN cupboard stall full of jars.
fr_ouvert_adj.why: Dressed rabbit replaced by a girl.

fr_faible_adj.hook: "FEHBL": FEEBLE! A FEEBLE, WEAK little boy wobbles under the weight of a single big feather, while a sturdy boy flexes beside him.
fr_faible_adj.why: Animals replaced by children; English sound-alike FEEBLE.

fr_ferme_adj_2.hook: A little wooden shed is CLOSED ("fehr-MAY"), its doors shut with a big padlock: no fair in May, come back tomorrow.
fr_ferme_adj_2.why: Reworded to match the painting: the closed thing is a padlocked shed, not a sign.

fr_vrai_adj.hook: A wise old donkey BRAYS ("VREH") "TRUE! TRUE!" when an honest boy holding a flowerpot tells the truth.
fr_vrai_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: the honest boy with his flowerpot stands beside the donkey. Text pass 2026-10-28: bracketed respelling matched to the card (VRAY -> VREH).

fr_gros_adj.hook: A BIG fat pumpkin keeps GROWing ("GROH") in the garden until it squashes the fence.

fr_heureux_adj.hook: A HAPPY puppy gets a brand-new red ball and barks "HURRAH!" ("euh-REUH"), spinning in circles.
fr_heureux_adj.why: kept, matches the painting. Text pass 2026-10-28 (hook lint): respelling (uh-RUH) -> (euh-REUH) to match the card.

fr_faux_adj.hook: A FAKE foe ("FOH") in a false mustache: the mustache flies off, and he's just the mailman.

fr_triste_adj.hook: A tree ("TREEST") stands SAD in the rain under its own little cloud, branches drooping.
fr_triste_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: the sad tree is a willow under a rain cloud.

fr_large_adj.hook: A tailor measures a sofa: not "large", WIDE! The tape stretches from one end to the other.

fr_malheureux_adj.hook: At the MALL, nobody shouts HURRAH ("mah-leuh-REUH") for the UNHAPPY clown whose balloons all popped: only scraps are left.
fr_malheureux_adj.why: kept, matches the painting. Text pass 2026-10-28 (hook lint): respelling (ma-luh-RUH) -> (mah-leuh-REUH) to match the card.

fr_mince_adj.hook: A THIN praying MANTIS ("MANCE") slips easily through the mail slot of a green front door.
fr_mince_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: the door is painted green.

fr_etroit_adj.hook: "A trois!" ("ay-TRWAH"): three cats squeeze one behind the other through a NARROW gap by the gate post.
fr_etroit_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: the narrow place is a gap by the gate post, not an alley.

fr_gai_adj.hook: A CHEERFUL goat rides on a swinging GATE ("GEH"), singing a happy song.

fr_possible_adj.hook: Like English 'possible', said poh-SEEBL: a POSSE of ants proves it's POSSIBLE to carry a whole sandwich along the jetty.
fr_possible_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: they carry it along the wooden jetty.

fr_dur_adj.hook: Like English 'durable', said DEWR: a DOUR beaver bites a rock on the bank, and his teeth go "boing": it's far too HARD.
fr_dur_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: the beaver sits on the bank.

fr_clair_adj.hook: Like English 'clear', said KLEHR: CLAIRE holds up a CLEAR glass of water; you can see right through it.

fr_doux_adj.hook: A white dove coos "DOO" as it settles on a SOFT, fluffy pillow on the jetty.
fr_doux_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: the pillow lies on the jetty.

fr_impossible_adj.hook: Like English 'impossible', said an-poh-SEEBL: a pig in paper wings attempts the IMPOSSIBLE flight over the pond while ducks hold up score cards.
fr_impossible_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: the score cards are blank (no text).

fr_calme_adj.hook: "KAHLM": CALM grandpa dozes in his deckchair, hands folded, while the pond bustles around him.
fr_calme_adj.why: Tortoise in sunglasses replaced by a grandfather; cognate CALM.

fr_cher_adv.hook: "Share? ("SHEHR") No, too EXPENSIVE!" gasps a DEAR old lady at the huge price tag on a teapot.
fr_cher_adv.why: Reworded to match the painting: the price tag is blank (no text) and hangs from a teapot.

fr_sombre_adj.hook: Like English 'somber', said SOHNBR: a lamplighter climbs his ladder to the only lamp glowing under a DARK, shady tree.
fr_sombre_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: the dark place is a shady tree with one lamp, not a street.

fr_nerveux_adj.hook: "nehr-VEUH": NERVY! A NERVOUS chihuahua shivers, teeth chattering, beside the calm grandpa.

fr_gratuit_adj.hook: "Great, wee!" ("grah-TWEE"): a smiling vendor hands out a FREE ice cream and a toddler cheers.
fr_gratuit_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: the vendor hands the cone over; there is no sign.

fr_beau_adj.hook: A HANDSOME prince in a red cape straightens his bow ("BOH") tie and admires himself in a standing mirror.

fr_gentil_adj.hook: Not quite "gentle": gentil (zhahn-TEE) means KIND, NICE; a little boy holds his umbrella over an old man.
fr_gentil_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: the stranger is an old man.

fr_sec_adj.hook: A camel carries a SACK ("SEHK") across DRY, cracked ground without a drop of water.
fr_sec_adj.why: kept, matches the painting. Text pass 2026-10-28: bracketed respelling matched to the card (SEK -> SEHK).

fr_proche_adj.hook: A cat creeps CLOSE to a posh ("PROSH") crystal fishbowl on a stool, eyeing the goldfish.
fr_proche_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: the posh thing is the fancy crystal bowl; the cat wears no collar.

fr_lointain_adj.hook: A lion ("LWAN") with a tan lounges on a DISTANT island far out on the lake.

fr_mechant_adj.hook: "may-SHAHN": they MAY SHUN him! A MEAN black cat nips the dog from behind and the dog yelps; the other animals may shun that cat.
fr_mechant_adj.why: Cat no longer wears a top hat and ruff (natural cat).

fr_silencieux_adj.hook: Like English 'silent', said see-lahn-SYEUH: a SILENT owl sits on its post with eyes half shut, while the goose beside it honks.
fr_silencieux_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: the owl is shown sitting still and quiet.

fr_laid_adj.hook: An UGLY but friendly warty troll LAYS ("LEH") his big hands on the quay wall and grins up from the lake.
fr_laid_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: he leans his hands, not his chin, on the stone quay wall.

fr_mouille_adj.hook: A WET shaggy dog shakes water all over a cow ("MOO") who shouts "YAY!" ("moo-YAY") and laughs.

fr_bruyant_adj.hook: NOISY Bryan ("brwee-YAHN") bangs a pot with a wooden spoon while his family covers their ears.
fr_bruyant_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: he bangs one pot with a spoon.

fr_simple_adj.hook: Like English 'simple', said SANPL: a chef offers a SIMPLE SAMPLE: just a plain cracker on a plate.
fr_simple_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: he offers plain crackers on a plate on the bank.

fr_present_adj.hook: Like English 'present', said pray-ZAHN: little ZAN shoots up her hand on the footbridge, "PRESENT!", as a teacher takes the register.

fr_rare_adj.hook: Like English 'rare', said RAHR: a RARE golden frog on the footbridge is cheered "RAH!" by two bird-watchers with huge binoculars.
fr_rare_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: the bird-watchers are two birds with binoculars.

fr_moderne_adj.hook: Like English 'modern', said moh-DEHRN: a MODERN glass URN full of neon squiggles stands next to a cracked old Roman vase.

fr_traditionnel_adj.hook: Like English 'traditional', said trah-dee-syoh-NEHL: NELL in a TRADITIONAL lace bonnet and clogs dances toward a breakdancing robot.

fr_complique_adj.hook: Like English 'complicated', said kohn-plee-KAY: KAY untangles a COMPLICATED knot of fairy lights that has somehow wrapped itself round the cat.

fr_absent_adj.hook: Like English 'absent', said ahp-SAHN: an ABSENT-minded professor strolls along reading, wearing a teapot as a hat.
fr_absent_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: he walks past the footbridge reading a book.

fr_frequent_adj.hook: Like English 'frequent', said fray-KAHN: the pigeons make such FREQUENT visits to the old man's bench that he has named one "Kahn".
fr_frequent_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: the bench is surrounded by pigeons.
